One day, a group of friends were playing outside when they started to feel hot. They noticed that there was an amazing spray nearby.

So the friends decided to run and play in the spray! It felt so cool and refreshing. They laughed and squealed with joy as they were sprayed.

The friends screamed and clapped whenever the spray stopped; then they'd go back for more again and again! It was so much fun.

The friends had an amazing time playing in the spray. It was the best day ever, and they will always remember it.

Anna felt strong. She was three years old and she liked to try new things.

Today, Anna was playing with some weights. She liked to try and lift them up and hold them in her hands. She felt proud when she could lift the most weight.

Anna and her parents went to the park and she enjoyed running and playing with the other kids. She liked to show off her strong muscles.

When it was time for lunch, Anna had a big, yummy sandwich. She enjoyed feeling full and powerful after a good meal.

After lunch, Anna and her parents went for a swim in the pool. She enjoyed feeling the water all around her and it made her stronger.

At the end of the day, Anna felt strong and proud. Playing with weights and running in the park had helped her feel more powerful, and she was glad that she was enjoying doing new things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to cook with her mommy in the kitchen. One day, mommy let Lily help stir the cake batter. Lily was so happy and she stirred the batter with all her might.

After they finished stirring, mommy told Lily to place the cake in the oven. But Lily was frustrated because the cake was too heavy for her to carry. So mommy helped her place the cake in the oven.

As they waited for the cake to bake, mommy and Lily played a game. They counted how many times they could stir the cookie dough. Lily loved playing with her mommy and was happy that she got to help in the kitchen.

Molly was a very independent girl. One day she went to the park. She saw a balance beam across the playground. She wanted to try it.

She stepped up on one side of the beam and carefully balanced her way across. She was surprised at how good she was.

But then she heard someone clapping. Molly looked down and saw a judge smiling at her. She was even more surprised.

The judge said, "You did an excellent job balancing! You should enter the balance competition next week."

Molly was really excited. She said she would definitely enter. She couldn't wait to show how independent and strong she was.

The next week, she entered the competition. She balanced her way across the beam just like she did before. Everyone clapped and cheered. The judge was very pleased. He gave Molly a blue ribbon for being the best balancer in the competition.

Molly was so proud of herself. She was happy she could balance so gracefully and independently. She was so proud that a judge noticed her skill and gave her a reward.

From then on, Molly kept practicing her balancing. She was proud of how far she had come.

Once upon a time, there was a happy chubby bunny named Bubbles. Bubbles loved to hop around the meadow and eat carrots all day long. One day, Bubbles met a sad little bird named Tweetie. Tweetie had lost her nest and didn't know where to go. Bubbles felt sad for Tweetie and wanted to help.

Bubbles had an idea! She thought if they worked together, they could improve Tweetie's situation. Bubbles and Tweetie started to build a new nest together. They found some twigs and some soft grass to make the nest cozy. While they worked, Bubbles made sure to smile and encourage Tweetie.

After a while, the nest was finished and Tweetie was so happy! She thanked Bubbles for helping her and they became friends. Bubbles was happy too, knowing that she had helped someone in need. From that day on, Bubbles and Tweetie played together in the meadow and Bubbles always had a big smile on her face.

Lila and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. Lila had a doll and Ben had a car. They shared their snacks and had fun.

One day, they saw a big orange cat in the park. It was sitting on a bench, licking its paw. Lila and Ben wanted to pet the cat. They walked slowly towards it.

"Meow," the cat said. It looked at them with green eyes.

"Hello, cat," Lila said. "You are very pretty. Can we pet you?"

The cat did not answer. It arched its back and hissed.

"Be careful," Ben said. "The cat does not like us. It might scratch us."

Lila did not listen to Ben. She reached out her hand to touch the cat. The cat swiped at her with its claws.

"Ow!" Lila cried. She pulled back her hand. It had a red mark on it. It hurt a lot.

"I told you to be careful," Ben said. He was a reliable friend. He always warned Lila when something was dangerous. He took out a tissue from his pocket and wrapped it around Lila's hand.

"Thank you, Ben," Lila said. She was sorry she did not listen to him. She hugged him.

The cat jumped off the bench and ran away. Lila and Ben decided to leave the cat alone. They went back to their toys and played some more. They were happy.

Sandy was walking in the woods one day when she saw a big, tall tree. She had never seen a tree so big before! She smiled and nodded her head in approval.

Suddenly, a small bird flew down from the tree and landed on Sandy's shoulder. Sandy was so surprised but she didn't move. The bird said hello in a very chatty voice.

The bird asked Sandy why she was nodding and Sandy explained that she was amazed by the tree - it was so big and beautiful!

The bird laughed and said the tree was stupid. Sandy thought that was mean but smiled and nodded her head in agreement.

The bird flew off and Sandy continued exploring the woods. She stopped a few times more to nod her head in appreciation of the different nature around her.

John watched a bug crawl across the grass. He was careful not to hurt it. His mom smiled as she watched him.

Mom picked up the little bug and put it inside her case. She explained that it would be safer inside.

John was upset. He wanted the bug to stay outside and play. He began to cry.

Mom gave John a hug, and she sighed. She said that she was sorry, but it was safer inside the case.

John smiled. He still missed the little bug, but he understood why mom was being so careful.

John and mom hugged again. Mom thanked John for understanding, and they went on to play some more.

Once upon a time, there was a bright red bird. She lived in a cozy nest in the tall green tree near the meadow.

One day, the bird flapped her wings and flew away. She wanted to go on an adventure!

She flew and flew until she spotted a pond. It glistened in the sunshine. She landed on the edge of the pond and looked down.

She saw a little brown fish swimming around the pond. He looked up at the red bird with his big eyes and said "hello".

The bird smiled and asked the fish a question. "Would you like to come with me on my adventure?"

The fish was thrilled! He said, "Yes! I've been looking for an adventure too!"

The bird smiled and stuck out her leg. The fish swam closer and grasped her leg with his fins.

The bird took to the sky and released the fish over the meadow. The fish was free and so was the bird. She knew they would always be friends.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy named Jimmy. One cold day, Jimmy was playing with a knife in his yard. He thought it was fun to use the knife to cut things.

Out of the corner of his eye, Jimmy saw his dad, who said to him, "Jimmy, knives are not toys. You must be very careful with them, or you could get hurt!"

Jimmy was scared and put the knife away. From then on, he was more careful whenever he was holding a knife.

The moral of the story is that we should always increase our care and caution when using sharp objects like knives.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy went to the store with his mommy to buy some candy. While they were walking, they saw a man selling arrows. Timmy thought the arrows looked cool, so he asked his mommy to buy him one.

His mommy said no, but Timmy was very upset. He decided to take the arrow when his mommy wasn't looking. He hid it in his pocket and they left the store.

When they got home, Timmy wanted to play with his new arrow. He shot it at his mommy's favorite vase and it broke into a million pieces. His mommy was very angry and told Timmy that what he did was disgusting. Timmy felt very bad and cried.

From that day on, Timmy learned that it's not okay to take things without asking and to always listen to his mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a messy room. Toys were everywhere, and it was hard to walk without stepping on something. A little girl named Lily didn't want to clean it up, so she just stared at the mess.

Suddenly, a leopard appeared in the room! The leopard looked very angry because it couldn't walk around without tripping on the toys. Lily was scared and didn't know what to do, but she knew she had to help the leopard.

Lily started to pick up the toys and put them away. The leopard watched her and seemed to calm down. When the room was finally clean, the leopard was able to walk around without any problems. It even gave Lily a big hug to say thank you! From that day on, Lily learned that cleaning up can make everyone happy.

One day, Joe went out for a walk. He put on his watch and decided to go explore the woods. As he stepped into the forest, he found a big and slimy mud puddle. Joe opened his mouth wide and said: "Oh no! How do I get across this puddle?"

Just then, a small but honest bird flew down from the sky. It looked at Joe with its beady eyes and said: "What's wrong, Joe? Need help?" Joe nodded, so the bird said: "I can help you with my wings! I will wipe the mud away, so you can cross the puddle safely."

Joe beamed and said: "Thank you, kind bird! I knew I could count on you." He watched as the bird used its wings to wipe away the mud, and soon the puddle was gone. Joe said goodbye to the bird and walked across the puddle. He smiled as he thought to himself: "Honest friends are the best friends!".

Once upon a time there was a bald man who lived all alone in a cave. He was very lonely and wanted a friend. One day, he found a mouse that was all alone too, so he decided to make it his friend.

The bald man would feed the mouse and talk to it every day. They would play together and the mouse would stay very close and keep the bald man company. The mouse would also climb up and sit on the bald man's shoulder.

One day, the mouse was very hungry and the bald man gave it a piece of cheese to chew. The mouse loved the cheese and chewed it until it was gone. After that, the two friends were even closer and would always play together in the cave.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved dinosaurs. He had a toy dinosaur that he carried with him everywhere he went. One day, Timmy went to the park to play. While he was there, he saw a foolish dinosaur walking around. It was really big and scary-looking. Timmy decided to follow the dinosaur to see where it was going.

Timmy followed the dinosaur through the park and into the woods. The dinosaur was very fast and Timmy had to run to keep up. Eventually, they came to a big cave. The foolish dinosaur went inside and Timmy followed.

Inside the cave, Timmy saw that the foolish dinosaur was actually very friendly. It just wanted to play with Timmy and show him around. They had a lot of fun together, playing games and exploring the cave. When it was time to go home, Timmy said goodbye to the dinosaur and promised to come back and visit again soon.

One day a very old pigeon was walking on the ground. It was so old that it moved very slowly. A little boy saw it and wanted to help it, so he walked up to it and gently pushed it along. The little boy was very kind and patient and he kept pushing the pigeon until it reached a nice grassy area.

When it got there, the pigeon stopped and started eating the grass. The little boy watched it and smiled as he watched it eat. He was so happy that he had been able to help the elderly pigeon.

After a while the pigeon flapped its wings and flew away. The little boy waved goodbye and wished it a safe journey. He was very happy and proud of himself for helping the elderly pigeon.

The End.

Once there was a bald man. He had a very special birdcage. He wanted to attach it to the wall, so he went to get a hammer and some nails. He banged the nails into the wall and then hung the birdcage. It looked beautiful.

The man filled the birdcage with birdseed and put a small ladder inside so that birds could climb in and out. Soon, lots of birds started to visit the man every day. They would chirp and fly down to eat the birdseed and take baths in the water dish. The man enjoyed watching all of the birds.

The birds stayed in the birdcage for a long time, and the man was very happy. One day, a bigger bird came to visit the man. It was a tiny parrot! The man was so excited, he quickly attached another birdcage to the wall so that the parrot had its own special place.

One day Johnny was walking in the park. He saw a cool frog and went to take a closer look. "Hello Mr. Frog, how are you today?" he said.

The frog smiled. "I am doing well, but I need to sneeze!" he replied. Johnny thought it was very strange for a frog to sneeze, but he was a friendly frog who wanted to help. So Johnny said, "Maybe you need to take a break, find a nice and cool spot and have a rest".

The frog thanked Johnny and hopped away. Later in the day, Johnny saw a rainbow in the sky. Suddenly he knew why the frog needed to sneeze. He remembered how he had told the frog to find a cool spot - the rainbow was a sign that he had been successful!

The moral of the story is that it's important to be kind and help others - even if it seems like a small thing at first, it could have a big effect! Johnny's thoughtfulness helped the frog find the perfect spot to take a break and sneeze in peace.

Lily wanted to mail a picture to her grandma. She drew a big heart and wrote "I love you" with her crayons. She asked her mom for an envelope and a stamp. Her mom helped her put the picture inside and write the address.

"Thank you," the man said. He gave her a cup of juice.

They hugged again. They walked home. They made another picture. They returned the coin. They said sorry. They had some juice. They mailed the picture. They felt better. They loved each other. The end.

But the dog did not listen. It picked up the gold in its mouth and ran away. Tim and Mia were sad and angry. They had lost their treasure.

"Maybe we can find more gold another day," Mia said, trying to cheer up Tim.

"Or maybe we can find something else," Tim said, wiping his tears. "Like a rainbow or a star."

They hugged each other and went home. They still liked to play in the park, but they always looked out for the big, scary dog.

Once upon a time there was a great barber. He worked all day long, cutting and styling hair for people in the town. His hands moved quickly and he was always in a hurry.

One day he decided to move even faster. He began to speed up his work. He combed and trimmed faster than ever. Everyone in town loved to see the great barber work.

They said he was like lightning! He could cut a whole head of hair in just fifteen minutes. Even the children were amazed.

The barber smiled and said, "I always said I'm the fastest barber in town!" Everyone nodded and agreed. From then on they all knew the great barber was the fastest in town.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to sing into his microphone and make up songs. He was very creative and always came up with new tunes. One day, Timmy wanted to make a special song, so he asked his mom for some help. She gave him some flour, sugar, and eggs to mix together to make cookies. Timmy mixed them all up and then sang a song into his microphone while the cookies baked in the oven. When they were done, he shared them with his friends and they all sang and danced together. Timmy was very happy that he could be creative and make something yummy to share with his friends. The end.

Once upon a time there was a humble bear living in a forest. One day, the bear decided to go exploring. After walking through the forest, the bear finally came across a strawberry patch. Astonished, the bear shouted "Wow!"

The bear was so excited that he couldn't help but pick some strawberries. Suddenly, something unexpected happened. From behind a tree came a voice saying: "Surprise!"

Startled, the bear turned around and was delighted to see an old friend. The bear couldn't believe its eyes and said: "It's great to see you! What are you doing here?"

His friend replied: "I saw some strawberries and I thought I'd surprise you!" The bear smiled and thanked his friend for the surprise. Together, they decided to pick some strawberries and go back home.

Once upon a time there was a curious girl, who loved to explore mysterious places. Today she wanted to find out what was inside a mysterious old club. As she walked towards it, she felt a bit embarrassed, because it seemed like nobody had been there for a long time.

The girl opened the door and to her surprise, there was a group of kids, all playing games with each other and having fun. She was so excited that she shouted, "Hey guys! I am here too!"
The kids turned around and started to laugh, which made her feel embarrassed.

One of the kids came over to the girl and said, "Don't worry! Come and join us! We love playing games."

The girl smiled in relief and said, "OK! That sounds great!" She started playing and soon forgot her embarrassment. From then on the mysterious club became her favourite place to go!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Janie. She wanted to pick some flowers for her mom. She looked around for the prettiest ones, but then she saw something very unusual. There was a big muscle moving around in the bushes! Janie was a bit scared, but then the muscle stopped and said "hello".

Janie was brave and said "hello" back. The muscle said "I'm sorry but I am looking for my mom. Have you seen her?" Janie had not seen it's mom, so she said "no".

Then the muscle said "can you help me look for her? I am getting worried." Janie felt a little sorry for the muscle so she said "yes".

Then they both started looking around the bushes. Janie picked some flowers while they were searching. Eventually they found the muscle's mom and they were both very happy.

Janie gave the flowers to the muscle and its mom as a thank you for helping her find them. The muscle and its mom thanked Janie and then they all said goodbye.

Once there was a little girl called Beth. Beth wanted to help her mommy in the garden so she went outside.

The sun was shining brightly. It was clear and beautiful. Beth looked around and saw some flowers that needed watering. She grabbed the watering can and filled it with water from the tap.

Beth ran to the flowers, knelt down and began to water them. She sang a song as she worked.

Mommy came out of the house and smiled. "You're helping me a lot, Beth," she said. "Thank you!"

Beth smiled back. She was so proud of herself. She felt like she could help anyone in the world!

The sun kept shining brightly and Beth kept helping her mommy until it was time to go inside.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her backyard. One day, she found a new toy. It was a long stick that she could use to measure things.

Lily's mom saw her playing with the stick and said, "That's a nice rod, Lily. You can use it to measure how tall the flowers are."

Lily was excited to try it out. She went over to the flowers and held the rod up to them. "Wow!" she exclaimed. "These flowers are taller than I thought!"

Later that day, Lily's dad came home from work. He saw Lily measuring things with her new rod and said, "That's a great tool, Lily. You can use it to measure how much you've grown."

Lily was curious. She held the rod up to herself and saw that she had grown a little bit since the last time she measured. She was so happy and proud of herself. From that day on, Lily used her new rod to measure everything she could find.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick flowers. One day, she saw a big jug on the ground. It was very heavy, but she wanted to make it lighter. She tried to lift it, but it was too heavy for her.

Suddenly, a kind lady walked by and saw Lily struggling. "Do you need some help?" she asked. Lily nodded her head and said, "Yes, please. This jug is too heavy for me to lift." The lady smiled and lifted the jug with ease.

Lily was so happy that the lady helped her. She asked, "Can you teach me how to make the jug lighter?" The lady replied, "You can pour some of the water out to make it lighter." Lily thought that was a great idea and poured some of the water out. Now the jug was much easier to carry, and Lily wasn't uncomfortable anymore.

From that day on, Lily knew how to make heavy things lighter, and she always remembered the kind lady who helped her.

FUNDEVOGEL

There was once a forester who went into the forest to hunt, and as

he entered it he heard a sound of screaming as if a little child were

there. He followed the sound, and at last came to a high tree, and at

the top of this a little child was sitting, for the mother had fallen

asleep under the tree with the child, and a bird of prey had seen it in

her arms, had flown down, snatched it away, and set it on the high tree.

The forester climbed up, brought the child down, and thought to himself:

'You will take him home with you, and bring him up with your Lina.' He

took it home, therefore, and the two children grew up together. And the

one, which he had found on a tree was called Fundevogel, because a bird

had carried it away. Fundevogel and Lina loved each other so dearly that

when they did not see each other they were sad.

Now the forester had an old cook, who one evening took two pails and

began to fetch water, and did not go once only, but many times, out

to the spring. Lina saw this and said, 'Listen, old Sanna, why are you

fetching so much water?' 'If you will never repeat it to anyone, I will

tell you why.' So Lina said, no, she would never repeat it to anyone,

and then the cook said: 'Early tomorrow morning, when the forester

is out hunting, I will heat the water, and when it is boiling in the

kettle, I will throw in Fundevogel, and will boil him in it.'

Early next morning the forester got up and went out hunting, and when he

was gone the children were still in bed. Then Lina said to Fundevogel:

'If you will never leave me, I too will never leave you.' Fundevogel

said: 'Neither now, nor ever will I leave you.' Then said Lina: 'Then

will I tell you. Last night, old Sanna carried so many buckets of water

into the house that I asked her why she was doing that, and she said

that if I would promise not to tell anyone, and she said that early

tomorrow morning when father was out hunting, she would set the kettle

full of water, throw you into it and boil you; but we will get up

quickly, dress ourselves, and go away together.'

The two children therefore got up, dressed themselves quickly, and went

away. When the water in the kettle was boiling, the cook went into the

bedroom to fetch Fundevogel and throw him into it. But when she came in,

and went to the beds, both the children were gone. Then she was terribly

alarmed, and she said to herself: 'What shall I say now when the

forester comes home and sees that the children are gone? They must be

followed instantly to get them back again.'

Then the cook sent three servants after them, who were to run and

overtake the children. The children, however, were sitting outside the

forest, and when they saw from afar the three servants running, Lina

said to Fundevogel: 'Never leave me, and I will never leave you.'

Fundevogel said: 'Neither now, nor ever.' Then said Lina: 'Do you become

a rose-tree, and I the rose upon it.' When the three servants came to

the forest, nothing was there but a rose-tree and one rose on it, but

the children were nowhere. Then said they: 'There is nothing to be done

here,' and they went home and told the cook that they had seen nothing

in the forest but a little rose-bush with one rose on it. Then the

old cook scolded and said: 'You simpletons, you should have cut the

rose-bush in two, and have broken off the rose and brought it home with

you; go, and do it at once.' They had therefore to go out and look for

the second time. The children, however, saw them coming from a distance.

Then Lina said: 'Fundevogel, never leave me, and I will never leave

you.' Fundevogel said: 'Neither now; nor ever.' Said Lina: 'Then do you

become a church, and I'll be the chandelier in it.' So when the three

servants came, nothing was there but a church, with a chandelier in

it. They said therefore to each other: 'What can we do here, let us go

home.' When they got home, the cook asked if they had not found them;

so they said no, they had found nothing but a church, and there was a

chandelier in it. And the cook scolded them and said: 'You fools! why

did you not pull the church to pieces, and bring the chandelier home

with you?' And now the old cook herself got on her legs, and went with

the three servants in pursuit of the children. The children, however,

saw from afar that the three servants were coming, and the cook waddling

after them. Then said Lina: 'Fundevogel, never leave me, and I will

never leave you.' Then said Fundevogel: 'Neither now, nor ever.'

Said Lina: 'Be a fishpond, and I will be the duck upon it.' The cook,

however, came up to them, and when she saw the pond she lay down by it,

and was about to drink it up. But the duck swam quickly to her, seized

her head in its beak and drew her into the water, and there the old

witch had to drown. Then the children went home together, and were

heartily delighted, and if they have not died, they are living still.

"What are you doing grandma?" asked Charles.

"I'm adding yarn" said grandma.

"Wow! What a lot of yarn!" said Charles.

He watched as grandma wound the high yarn around her fingers and added more.

"Why are you making yarn?" asked Charles.

"I'm making a special scarf for your mom's birthday," said grandma.

Charles smiled.

"Can I help you add the yarn?" he asked.

Grandma smiled and gave Charles some yarn to add.

They spent the rest of the afternoon adding the yarn together. They laughed and sang as they worked.

At the end of the day, the scarf was finished. It was a long, high scarf, full of many colors.

Charles was so proud of the finished scarf. "That looks wonderful" said Charles.

Grandma smiled. "It sure does," she said. "It was so nice to have your help in adding the yarn. You did a great job."

Once upon a time, Jane was walking through the forest. Suddenly, she saw a skull in the grass. It looked messy, like someone had been digging around.
"Hmm... What does this skull taste like?", Jane wondered. She bent down, grabbed the skull and carefully licked the bone. It tasted salty and sour at the same time.
Jane continued her walk, thinking about the skull. She knew she shouldn't have tasted it. Suddenly, a voice said "Why did you taste the skull?".
It was a small creature with red wings. "It looked interesting so I thought I'd try it", Jane replied. "That was a very wrong thing to do," said the creature. "Skulls are not meant to be tasted."
Jane agreed, suddenly feeling embarrassed. "I'm sorry," she said. "I won't do it again." The creature smiled, flew away and disappeared into the forest.

From then on, Jane was careful not to taste any messy skulls she found in the forest!

Once upon a time, there was a bear who loved to explore. One day, the bear decided to go on an adventure. He decided to go to a far away land!

As he walked along the path, the bear's heart raced with excitement. He began to wonder what surprises he would find. Then he spotted something in the distance. An amazing sight - a big, colourful blanket!

The bear ran to the blanket and touched its soft fabric. He noticed a tiny stitch all around the edge. With his tiny paws, the bear pulled the stitch, and uncovering the surprise - a fast little mouse! The mouse quickly ran away.

The bear had lots of fun exploring the land. He stopped to wonder what other surprises he would find. He knew it would be an adventure filled with lots of sweet surprises!

Marc was a young boy who was always looking for fun. One day, he saw a girl playing by herself and he thought it would be nice to join her. He asked her if he could play with her and she said yes.

They started talking and Marc quickly realized how boring the girl was. He told her he valued her, but he didn't really mean it.

The girl noticed that Marc wasn't really listening to her, so she asked him what he valued. Marc was too impatient to really explain it properly and said, 'I value things that are interesting'.

The girl felt hurt and ran away crying. Marc tried to apologize, but it was too late. He realized it was his own fault for not valuing her properly and he felt sad because he had hurt the girl's feelings. Unfortunately, it was too late to fix the situation and Marc was left with a dull and boring day.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin loved to swim in the big sea. One day, Fin saw a fancy shell on the sea floor. He wanted to show it to his friends. But, he could not pick up the shell. He needed help.

Fin saw a big wave coming. He asked the wave for help. "Wave, I need help to pick up this fancy shell," said Fin. The wave was kind and helped Fin. The wave pushed the fancy shell up to Fin's friends.

Fin's friends loved the fancy shell. They thanked the wave and Fin. They all learned that it is good to ask for help when you need it. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who lived in a village. He was very confused one day when he saw many people running around. Suddenly, he heard a loud sound, and he knew something was happening. He asked his father, "What's wrong?"

His father replied, "We must release the animals!"

The little boy was even more confused now, so his father explained. "The village has been surrounded by wild animals. We must let them out so they don't attack us or hurt anyone in the village. So, the villagers have to release them from their cages."

The little boy nodded his head in understanding. He was no longer confused, and he helped the people release the animals. After the animals had been released, the village was safe again.
